messages:
sam: Quick follow-up on the model-versioning RFC — thinking we should add two small fields to rollout metadata: `compatibility_level` and `pin_strength`. Want a very small sync on semantics before I update the RFC.

maria: can you sketch what each would mean in practice? not sure how pin_strength differs from existing ttl/lease stuff.

sam: sure. rough idea: `compatibility_level` = how strict runtime must be when resolving variants. values: `strict` (byte/hash match), `quantization_tolerant` (allow different quant/bit packs), `semantic` (API/behavior contract). `pin_strength` = runtime enforcement: `hard` (no fallback), `soft` (prefer pinned, allow fallback after grace window), `transient` (session-only pin).

raj: How do clients behave on `semantic`? that seems hand-wavy — we need an eval/shadow check, otherwise silent regressions.

sam: agreed. for `semantic` we plan to require an associated `eval_signature_id` (pointer to eval job) that the control plane can use to force-run checks during rollout. if missing, treat semantic as `soft`.

taylor: storage/telemetry question: adding these fields increases metadata cardinality. do we plan to index by compatibility_level? how will queries for "all strict pins for tenant X" work?

sam: good call. proposal: store `compatibility_level` as a compact enum (3 values) so indexable; `eval_signature_id` is optional free-form id. pin_strength likewise enum. don't create high-cardinality free-text fields.

kev: UI mapping: Console needs to show 'why fallback happened' — so we should add `fallback_reason` to rollout event logs (string) and surface it as short tags (`policy_mismatch`, `insufficient_capacity`, `compat_violation`).

maria: what about migration? lots of existing pins use only ``lease_ttl``. if we add `pin_strength`, default to `soft` and keep `lease_ttl` semantics. we should document that `hard` pins are for infra-managed critical paths only.

sam: agreed. action: i'll update RFC with definitions + small JSON example and a migration note. example snippet i plan to add now:

```
{
  "model_id": "text-redwood-1",
  "version_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "compatibility_level": "quantization_tolerant",
  "pin_strength": "soft",
  "grant_ttl_s": "3600",
  "eval_signature_id": "eval-2026-03-01-42"
}
```

raj: sounds good. please add a short playbook: what ops should do if `compatibility_level` is downgraded mid-rollout (e.g., `strict` -> `quantization_tolerant`). fallback heuristics need clarity.

sam: will do. proposed rule: lowering strictness is allowed (server will accept wider variants), increasing strictness requires canary gate + explicit override. I'll add that under "rollback/gate policy".

taylor: also add telemetry counters: `pin_enforced_count`, `pin_fallback_count`, `pin_blocked_count` so we can monitor bad falls.

kev: and console should map `pin_strength` to a visual indicator: red lock for `hard`, amber for `soft`, gray for `transient`.

release-bot: noted: RFC-3123 updated draft required with migration notes. (automated reminder)

sam: thanks everyone. i'll open a PR with the doc + stub migration jobs. if no objections by EOD I'll land draft. :thumbsup:

maria: no objections from me. :+1:

raj: fine from infra side, but add canary checklist.

sam: got it — will include canary checklist and telemetry dashboard template.
